title: The Moon
text:
There is so much solitude in that gold.

The moon of nights is not the moon

the first Adam saw. The long centuries

of human wakefulness have filled it

with ancient weeping. Look at it. It is your mirror.
editorial_note: The moon accumulates human vigilance and grief across time; the final imperatives remain plain so the cosmic image turns abruptly intimate.

title: Farewell
text:
Between my beloved and me there shall rise

three hundred nights like three hundred walls,

and the sea will be a magic between us.


There will be nothing but memories.

O afternoons merited by sorrow,

nights hopeful of seeing you,

fields along my road, firmament

I am seeing and losing…

Definitive as marble,

your absence will sadden other afternoons.
editorial_note: Amor is rendered as beloved to keep the separation embodied; the repeated afternoons bind present loss to the future permanence of absence.

title: A Courtyard
text:
With evening

the courtyard’s two or three colors grew weary.

Tonight the moon, the lucid circle,

does not command its space.

Courtyard, channeled sky.

The courtyard is the slope

down which the sky spills into the house.

Serene,

eternity waits at a crossroads of stars.

It is good to live in the dark friendship

of an entryway, a grapevine, and a cistern.
editorial_note: The courtyard is retained as domestic architecture and a channel for the infinite; zaguán and aljibe remain concrete features of the rioplatense house.

title: To a Cat
text:
Mirrors are no more silent,

nor the adventurous dawn more furtive;

beneath the moon, you are that panther

we are permitted to glimpse from afar.

Through the inscrutable workings of a divine

decree, we seek you in vain;

more remote than the Ganges and the sunset,

yours is the solitude, yours the secret.

Your back condescends to the lingering

caress of my hand. You have admitted,

from that eternity which is now oblivion,

the love of the wary hand.

You inhabit another time. You are master

of a realm enclosed like a dream.
editorial_note: The cat’s remoteness is metaphysical rather than merely aloof; condesciende and recelosa preserve the unequal treaty between sovereign animal and cautious human touch.

title: The Forward Trench Is a Boarding Ship upon the Steppe…
text:
The forward trench is upon the steppe a boarding ship

with pennants of hurrahs

middays explode in the eyes

Beneath banners of silence the multitudes pass

and the sun crucified in the sunsets

multiplies itself in the clamor

of the Kremlin towers

The sea will come swimming toward those armies

that will wrap their torsos

in all the prairies of the continent

In the wild horn of a rainbow

we shall proclaim their exploit

bayonets

bearing mornings on their points




Grecia Magazine
, 1920
editorial_note: The young Borges’s Ultraist collisions are kept syntactically abrupt; military, maritime, continental, and chromatic images remain superimposed without retrospective smoothing.

title: The Rain
text:
Abruptly the afternoon has brightened

because now the meticulous rain is falling.

It falls or fell. Rain is a thing

that surely happens in the past.


Whoever hears it fall has recovered

the time when fortunate chance

revealed to him a flower called the rose

and the curious color of the color red.


This rain that blinds the windowpanes

will gladden, in lost outskirts,

the black grapes of a vine in a certain


courtyard that no longer exists. The wet

afternoon brings me the voice, the longed-for voice,

of my father returning, who has not died.
editorial_note: The temporal correction cae o cayó becomes falls or fell; colorado retains its childlike revelation through the deliberately recursive color of the color red.

title: We Are the Rivers
text:
We are time. We are the famous

parable of Heraclitus the Obscure.

We are the water, not the hard diamond,

the water that is lost, not that which rests.


We are the river and we are that Greek

who looks at himself in the river. His reflection

changes in the water of the changing mirror,

in the crystal that changes like fire.


We are the vain, preordained river,

bound for its sea. Shadow has encircled it.

Everything has said goodbye, everything recedes.


Memory does not mint its coin.

And yet there is something that remains,

and yet there is something that laments.
editorial_note: The repeated somos sustains collective identity through time, river, philosopher, and reflection; queda and queja are echoed as remains and laments without forcing rhyme.

title: Things
text:
The cane, the coins, the key ring,

the docile lock, the belated

notes the few days I have left

will not read, the cards and the board,


a book and in its pages the faded

violet, monument to an afternoon

undoubtedly unforgettable and already forgotten,

the red western mirror in which burns


an illusory dawn. How many things—

prints, thresholds, atlases, goblets, nails—

serve us as tacit slaves,


blind and strangely stealthy!

They will endure beyond our oblivion;

they will never know that we have gone.
editorial_note: The catalog of intimate objects retains its syntax of deferred mortality; the things’ service is followed by their greater duration and complete ignorance of human absence.
